US Mint Locations in the US (website)

requirements.text: Explain the following terms: obverse, reverse, reeding, clad, type set, and date set.

resources.title: Coin Collecting for Beginners; Coin Terminology and Coin Anatomy (video)

requirements.text: Describe three different ways to store a collection, and the benefits, drawbacks, and cost of each method.

resources.title: Coin Storage Tips | How and Where to Keep Your Collection Safe (video)

requirements.text: Do the following and explain to your counselor the design features, designer name, designer initials, and where to find them for each item:

resources.title: Coin Collecting 101 for Beginners: What You Need to Know to Start Coin Collecting (video)

children.label: (a)
children.text: Collect a one-cent coin from the year group: 1959-2008 (that is, dated between 1959 and 2008) and a one-cent coin from the year group 2010-present. Explain how and why the one-cent coins issued in 2009 were different from either of the other two year groups.

children.label: (b)
children.text: Collect two five-cent coins, one from each of these year groups: 1959-2003 and 2006-present. Explain how and why the five-cent coins issued in 2004-2005 were different from either of the other two year groups.

children.label: (d)
children.text: Collect a twenty-five-cent coin from 1965-1998, two examples from the 50-State Quarter®/territories Program 1999-2009, two designs from the America the Beautiful® program 2010-2021 and two designs from the American Women Quarter® program (2022-2024). Explain the purpose of each of those programs.

children.label: (e)
children.text: Collect a half dollar coin from 1965-present.

children.label: (f)
children.text: Collect a dollar coin from each of the following design groups: Susan B. Anthony (1979-1981, 1999); Sacagawea (2000-2008); and U.S. Presidents (2007-2016, 2020).

requirements.text: Describe and discuss with your counselor the special reverse designs of the quarters, half dollar, and dollar coin struck in 1975-1976 to honor the U.S. Bicentennial.
Identify for your counselor the people depicted on current currency: $1, $2, $5, $10, $20, $50, and $100 notes. Explain where United States currency is printed.

resources.title: Do You Know Who Is on Every US Banknote? (video)

children.label: (a)
children.text: Collect and identify for your counselor 20 different world coins from at least seven different countries. Identify the country, major design elements, and denomination of each.

children.label: (b)
children.text: Collect and identify for your counselor 20 different world paper money from at least seven different countries. Identify the country, major design elements, and denomination of each.

children.label: (c)
children.text: Collect and identify for your counselor 20 different tokens and/or medals. Identify the issuer and use of each.

children.label: (d)
children.text: Complete one of the following and report to your counselor what you experienced:

resources.title: National and Regional Coin Shows for Collectors (website)

children.text: Tour a U.S. Mint facility or museum

resources.title: US Mint Locations in the US (website)
